target.title: fix(voice-call): resolve completed calls from the persisted store on status misses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the `voice_call` tool's `get_status` action (and the legacy `status` mode / `voicecall.status` gateway method) reported `{ found: false }` for calls that had completed successfully and had a full transcript persisted to disk. Once a call was evicted from the in-memory call manager (after finalize, a gateway restart, or max-duration expiry), the lookups only checked memory and never fell back to the persisted store, so the agent could not retrieve the conversation that happened.

## Why This Change Was Made

All three status-lookup sites now fall back to the persisted call history when the in-memory manager has no entry, resolving the NEWEST matching snapshot. History is returned oldest-first, so the lookup uses `toReversed().find(...)` — a forward `find()` would return a stale/older snapshot. This mirrors the existing `describeHistoricalCall` helper, which already does the same persisted-history lookup.

Note: there is an existing PR #96624 with the same direction; it has been inactive since 2026-06-30 and its persisted fallback selects the oldest snapshot via `events.find()`, which can report stale/nonterminal state for a completed call. This change resolves the newest snapshot instead.

## User Impact

Operators and agents can retrieve the status and transcript of completed voice calls after they leave the in-memory manager (e.g. after a gateway restart or enough time has passed), instead of a dead-end `{ found: false }`.

## Evidence

- Two regression tests in `extensions/voice-call/index.test.ts`: one asserts the newest snapshot wins when history contains both a `ringing` and a `completed` record for the same call; one asserts `{ found: false }` when the call is neither active nor persisted.
- `pnpm test:extension voice-call` targeted run: `index.test.ts` 41/41 pass, including both new tests. The full extension suite only has pre-existing Windows `EPERM` teardown flakes in `src/manager/events.test.ts` (temp-dir `fs.rmSync`), unrelated to this change.

🤖 AI-assisted. Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code).

Closes #96586
